summary: Host-agent Literature Scout inspected Huang-Li v2 hypotheses and moving-cutoff rearrangement and Friedlander-Iwaniec's exact parity-breaking bilinear axiom. The endpoint maximum is essential, and the dropped cutoff is visible in the primary text. A located Moya preprint announces the same repair, but its PDF could not be retrieved, so detailed repair verification remains open. The report proposes an endpoint-aware transfer lemma and proves an elementary warning that the sparse prime-deletion transplant loses ordinary Mobius inversion on ambient integers. No Goldbach proof, quantitative EH for the deletion model, or novelty claim is established. No usage measurements were available.

claims.text: Huang-Li's inspected v2 twisted EH hypothesis includes max over y<N, von Mangoldt times reflected ordinary Mobius weights, own-global-sum centering and arbitrary logarithmic saving; the conditional Goldbach result is Corollary 1 in this version.
Under k=(N-n)/d, d>eta requires n<N-eta*k. The primary text's equation (18) drops this moving cutoff. This is an algebraic identity issue, not a disproof of its conditional theorem.

An O(log N) maximal-discrepancy transfer bound should repair the moving-endpoint AP replacement. It is proposed for separate theorem-author proof and independent review; a located 2026 preprint announces overlapping repair.

Friedlander-Iwaniec's asymptotic sieve uses an additional absolute-outer-sum Mobius bilinear axiom, beyond its ordinary remainder distribution hypotheses. Those conditions have not been verified for this reflected Goldbach sequence.
Leading prime density preserved by sparse deletion does not establish all-log-saving ordinary EH or BV; ordinary q=1 sees deleted weighted mass, whereas self-centered twisted q=1 is identically zero.

For allowed p and deleted r, -sum_{d|pr} mu_A(d) log d=log p but Lambda_A(pr)=0. Thus failure of Goldbach in the deletion model does not alone prove failure of a naively transplanted Huang-Li twisted hypothesis.
